start_here: Say to your AI: "Set how many customers I want for a product, so progress toward that target can be tracked", with {"product_id":"product:coaching","product_name":"Coaching","customers":10}. It runs tool:set-a-customer-target and answers {"target_id":"target:product:coaching","target_record":{"kind":"customer-product-target","targetId":"target:product:coaching","productId":"product:coaching","productLabel":"Coaching","targetCount":10,"active":true}}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Set how many customers I want for a product, so progress toward that target can be tracked", and give it product_id (The product's id, as your customer steps name it); product_name (The product's name); customers (How many customers the product aims for).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:set-a-customer-target and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Keeps the target in your own customer records (one per product; setting it again replaces it) and returns it; see-where-each-customer-is counts the product's customers against it.
